paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: you can stand on what you've been told about Jesus. Peter says he and the others did not follow "cleverly devised fables." They were "eyewitnesses of His majesty," and they heard the voice say, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." (2 Peter 1:16-17) So your faith isn't built on a rumor that got passed down the line.

Then Peter hands you a second thing to stand on, the word of the prophets, "confirmed beyond doubt." He says to pay attention to it "as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts." (2 Peter 1:19) I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so I'm telling you, a lamp in the dark is no small thing. And he says it comes from God, because "men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit." (2 Peter 1:21)

That's why Peter keeps reminding people who already know these things. (2 Peter 1:12) Even solid faith needs refreshing, because we forget, and the dark has a way of making us forget faster. So keep coming back to the Word, baker, and let that lamp keep shining on your path. It's the same lamp every time you open it, and it will keep shining until that day dawns.
